design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 04 → 4D « MONSTRE · création à la volée »: identity (NOM + visuel deferred), CARACTÉRISTIQUES (PV / ATTAQUE / DÉFENSE), outcome reveal texts, BUTIN LÂCHÉ (loot via shared ObjectEditor), « Ajouter à la librairie du générateur » (reusable across books). Combat outcomes resolve to réussite/échec — the only semantic colours (green/red), per § 05. Mounted via node-editor's « Action requise » seam. Low-fi wireframe.

plan.goal: Let an author configure a node's « Monstre » action — the monster's name and the player-facing reveal text for each combat outcome (réussite / échec) — mounted via the ActionRegistry, with a stub to save the monster to a reusable library.
acceptance_criteria: action-monster self-registers a « Monstre » editor with the brain ActionRegistry; node-editor's « Action requise » control offers « Monstre » alongside « Décor »/« PNJ » with zero node-editor changes (Open/Closed, KR-051).
Selecting « Monstre » mounts the editor for that node; structural screens (sommaire/mort) never show it.
The editor captures the monster name + a player-facing reveal text for EACH of the two outcomes; both are persisted on the node via BookService.

The two outcomes are réussite and échec — the only semantic outcomes — rendered with the only semantic colours (réussite = good/green, échec = bad/red), derived from the brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (KR-117), never hardcoded or branched on.

A « Ajouter à la librairie du générateur » affordance emits monster:savedToLibrary{bookId,nodeId} on the brain event bus (library stub; the reusable-monster catalog + persistence is a later iteration).

All monster config is persisted through BookService.updateNode (no private copy, KR-020) and lives on the node document; action-monster and node-editor never import each other (wired at the composition root).

The editor renders strictly from design-system primitives/tokens (Field, Badge good/bad), light theme; controls are keyboard-operable with ≥44px targets and the outcome fields carry an accessible name.
plan.walking_skeleton: registerActionMonster registers an ActionEditor { type:'monstre', label:'Monstre', render } with the brain ActionRegistry (wired at the App composition root). MonsterEditor reads node.monster live via useOpenBook and writes via BookService.updateNode: a NAME Field, and for each RollOutcome from the brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry a good/bad Badge + a reveal-text Field. « Ajouter à la librairie » emits monster:savedToLibrary. Stats (PV/Attaque/Défense), loot, combat-reinforced-by-object, outcome targets, and the real library are later iterations.

iterations.goal: Combat mechanics (§ 4D): PV / Attaque / Défense stats; outcome targets (victoire → poursuit / fuite → reliaison) wired through edges; defeat → Mort (the automatic combat path, KR-067).
Loot (« butin lâché ») via the shared ObjectEditor + combat reinforced by an inventory object (« si le joueur possède … alors victoire automatique »).
Reusable monster library via a MonsterLibraryService (« créer / librairie du générateur », reusable across books), consumed from the monster:savedToLibrary event.

known_risks: KR-050/051 — node-editor is a host: action-monster self-registers via the ActionRegistry and is mounted without being imported; adding the action needs zero node-editor changes.

KR-091 — combat/skill outcomes are réussite/échec ONLY, the only semantic colours; their label + tone live in the brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (KR-117) and the editor derives both outcomes from it — never hardcode « Réussite »/« Échec » or branch on the value. ROLL_OUTCOMES sits in brain because trap/skill-roll editors will reuse it (KR-109).
KR-020 — monster config is read/written through BookService (the SSOT); the editor holds no private copy and reflects live via useOpenBook.
KR-090 — monster config lives on the node document (node.monster); structural screens never carry it (updateNode's text-only guard for sommaire/mort, KR-055).
KR-013 — derive the editor's current values inline from the live node, not via a useEffect-synced mirror.
monster:savedToLibrary is wired as a contract now but has no consumer/persistence yet (library stub) — the real MonsterLibraryService lands in iteration 3, like the deferred Object/PNJ catalogs.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: Third action-* feature: self-registers with the brain ActionRegistry at the App composition root (registerActionMonster) — the seam now mounts three editors (« Décor »/« PNJ »/« Monstre ») with zero node-editor changes (KR-050/051).

réussite/échec — the only semantic outcomes — modelled as a brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (Record<RollOutcome,{label,tone}>, KR-117) placed in brain because trap/skill-roll editors will reuse it (KR-109). MonsterEditor derives BOTH outcome rows from it (good/bad Badge + reveal Field), no hardcoded labels/branches.
MonsterEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020): reads node.monster via useOpenBook, normalised once (DEFAULT_MONSTER + the cleaned pattern), writes via updateNode.

The monster-library is stubbed via a new monster:savedToLibrary event on the brain EventBus (per CLAUDE.md's event list) — wired now, consumed later. Added ariaLabel to the shared Field so the Badge-captioned outcome fields keep an accessible name.
deviations_from_plan: Stats (PV/Attaque/Défense), loot, combat-reinforced-by-object, outcome targets, and the real reusable-monster library are deferred to iterations 1–3; the skeleton ships name + réussite/échec reveal texts + the library-event stub.

test_coverage.integration: action-monster via App — « Monstre » offered through the registry seam, name + both réussite/échec outcome texts persisted, « Ajouter à la librairie » emits monster:savedToLibrary; structural-screen guard now covers monster (BookService)

open_questions: Combat stats + outcome targets + defeat→Mort automatic path (iteration 1).
Loot + combat-reinforced-by-object (iteration 2); reusable MonsterLibraryService consuming monster:savedToLibrary (iteration 3).
